formulation/kumkumadi-thailam#180.claimedTitle: Mixed sandalwood-saffron formulations and skin barrier repair
formulation/kumkumadi-thailam#180.finding: Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology reported that sandalwood-[saffron](/nighantu/herb/saffron/) formulations significantly reduce transepidermal water loss (TEWL), supporting skin barrier repair and validating the synergistic effects of Kumkumadi's key ingredients.

formulation/kutajarishta#181.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/kutajarishta#181.claimedTitle: Clinical trial of Kutajarishta efficacy against Entamoeba histolytica
formulation/kutajarishta#181.finding: Documented efficacy against E. histolytica, reducing stool frequency by up to 60% within 5 days in patients with amoebic dysentery.

formulation/kutajarishta#182.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/kutajarishta#182.claimedTitle: Randomized controlled trial of Kutajarishta versus loperamide
formulation/kutajarishta#182.finding: Similar stool consistency normalization compared to loperamide but with faster digestive comfort improvement in the Kutajarishta group, suggesting superior tolerability.

formulation/kutajarishta#183.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/kutajarishta#183.claimedTitle: Antidiarrhoeal mechanisms of Kutajarishta: antimotility and antisecretory effects
formulation/kutajarishta#183.finding: Antidiarrheal effect acts through potassium channels and nitric oxide pathway, not through alpha-2 adrenergic receptors. Produces combined antisecretory and antimotility effects.

formulation/kutajarishta#184.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/kutajarishta#184.claimedTitle: Pharmacological evaluation of Kutajarishta action on intestinal motility
formulation/kutajarishta#184.finding: Experimental study confirmed dose-dependent reduction in intestinal motility. Conessine, the major steroidal alkaloid from Kutaja bark, inhibits bacterial adenylate cyclase, reducing secretory diarrhea.

formulation/lakshadi-thailam#185.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#185.claimedTitle: Traditional knowledge review of Lakshadi Thailam in paediatric bone and muscle development
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#185.finding: Comprehensive review of traditional evidence and modern pharmacological data on individual ingredients confirmed that [Ashwagandha](/nighantu/herb/ashwagandha/), [Turmeric](/nighantu/herb/turmeric/), and Lac resin possess bone-strengthening, anti-inflammatory, and [immunomodulatory](/nighantu/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties relevant to infant development.

formulation/lakshadi-thailam#186.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#186.claimedTitle: Antimicrobial and skin-protective evaluation of Lakshadi Thailam ingredients
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#186.finding: Individual ingredient analysis confirmed that [Nirgundi](/nighantu/herb/nirgundi/), Nutgrass, and Licorice extracts possess significant antibacterial activity against common infant skin pathogens, supporting its traditional use for skin infection prevention in infants.

formulation/lakshadi-thailam#187.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#187.claimedTitle: Calcium-binding and osteogenic potential of Lac resin (Laksha) in bone tissue models
formulation/lakshadi-thailam#187.finding: In vitro studies demonstrated that Lac resin components promote calcium deposition in osteoblast cultures and may support bone mineralization, providing a scientific basis for the traditional claim of bone-strengthening in children.

formulation/lavangadi-vati#188.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lavangadi-vati#188.claimedTitle: Lavangadi Vati - An Ayurvedic Epitome for Communicable respiratory diseases
formulation/lavangadi-vati#188.finding: Comprehensive evaluation demonstrated [antipyretic](/nighantu/reference/antipyretic/), antiallergic, immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic properties relevant to respiratory infections.

formulation/lavangadi-vati#189.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lavangadi-vati#189.claimedTitle: In vitro antimicrobial assay of Lavangadi Vati extract
formulation/lavangadi-vati#189.finding: Extract demonstrated inhibitory zones against Streptococcus mutans and Staphylococcus aureus, validating potential in oral and respiratory infection management.

formulation/lavangadi-vati#190.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/lavangadi-vati#190.claimedTitle: Development and Evaluation of Lavangadi Vati in modified dosage form
formulation/lavangadi-vati#190.finding: Pharmaceutical development study explored optimized delivery forms maintaining the formulation's demulcent, anti-inflammatory, and expectorant properties while improving patient compliance.

formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#191.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#191.claimedTitle: A comparative clinical study to evaluate the effect of Madhusnuhi Rasayana and Shiva Gutika in Kitibha Kushta with special reference to psoriasis
formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#191.finding: [Madhusnuhi Rasayana](/nighantu/formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana/) demonstrated significant efficacy in managing Kitibha Kushta (psoriasis), comparable to Shiva Gutika in clinical outcomes

formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#192.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#192.claimedTitle: Pharmaceutical study on Brihat Madhusnuhi Rasayana
formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#192.finding: Pharmaceutical feasibility validated with organoleptic evaluation confirming consistent quality in standardized preparation methods

formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#193.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/madhusnuhi-rasayana#193.finding: Smilax china demonstrated anti-inflammatory, anti-rheumatic, anti-syphilitic, and blood-purifying activities supporting traditional [Rasayana](/nighantu/reference/rasayana/) claims

formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#194.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#194.claimedTitle: Clinical efficacy of Mahanarayana Thailam Abhyanga in osteoarthritis of knee
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#194.finding: Published in AYU Journal, the study reported 68% symptom reduction in osteoarthritic knee patients receiving Abhyanga with Mahanarayana Thailam over 21 days of treatment.

formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#195.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#195.claimedTitle: Anti-inflammatory and analgesic evaluation of Mahanarayana Taila polyherbal formulation
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#195.finding: Pharmacological analysis confirmed the presence of saponins, lignans, and phenolics that exert anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/) effects through COX-2 inhibition and free radical scavenging pathways.

formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#196.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#196.claimedTitle: Transdermal delivery efficacy of Mahanarayana Thailam in joint disorders
formulation/maha-narayana-thailam#196.finding: The lipid medium (sneha) of the formulation facilitated superior transdermal delivery of lipophilic phytoconstituents, resulting in higher tissue concentrations of active compounds at joint sites compared to simple oil application.

formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#197.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#197.claimedTitle: Validation and quantification of major biomarkers in Mahasudarshan Churna through high-performance thin-layer chromatography
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#197.finding: Developed validated HPTLC method for quantification of [mangiferin](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-l-o/#mangiferin) (xanthonoid), oleanolic acid and ursolic acid ([triterpenoids](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-t-z/#triterpenoids)), gallic acid, [quercetin](/nighantu/reference/quercetinquercetin/), and [curcumin](/nighantu/herb/curcumin/) as biomarkers in the formulation.
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#197.actualTitle: Validation and quantification of major biomarkers in 'Mahasudarshan Churna'- an ayurvedic polyherbal formulation through high-performance thin-layer chromatography

formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#198.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#198.claimedTitle: PLOS One pilot study on antipyretic efficacy of Sudarshan/Mahasudarshan formulations
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#198.finding: Pilot study found 25% faster drop in fever among subjects taking 3g twice daily compared to placebo.

formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#199.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#199.claimedTitle: Pharmacological studies on antipyretic, antimicrobial, antioxidant, antihistamine, and analgesic activities of Sudarshan Churna
formulation/mahasudarshan-churna#199.finding: Various pharmacological studies proved antipyretic, antimicrobial, antioxidant, antihistamine, and analgesic activities, plus docking studies against SARS-CoV-2 targets.

formulation/mahayograj-guggul#200.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/mahayograj-guggul#200.finding: Identified and quantified gallic acid, protocatechuic acid, vanillic acid, cinnamic acid, piperine, guggulsterone-E, guggulsterone-Z, ferulic acid, ellagic acid, and picroside I across six commercial batches, providing scientific basis for quality control.

formulation/mahayograj-guggul#201.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/mahayograj-guggul#201.finding: 60 patients over 12 weeks showed the full-spectrum formula group had 30% greater reduction in DAS28 scores (Disease Activity Score) with fewer gastrointestinal complaints than the extract-only group.

formulation/mahayograj-guggul#202.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/mahayograj-guggul#202.claimedTitle: UHPLC and GC-MS/MS authentication of quality reproducibility in Mahayograj Guggul
formulation/mahayograj-guggul#202.finding: Analytical methods employing UHPLC and GC-MS/MS provide validated reference for quality control evaluation of [Mahayograj Guggul](/nighantu/formulation/mahayograj-guggul/) and similar traditional broad-spectrum formulations.

formulation/murivenna#203.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/murivenna#203.claimedTitle: Wound healing potential of Murivenna in excision wound model
formulation/murivenna#203.finding: In-vivo study at Kerala University showed Murivenna Thailam enhanced collagen deposition in rat incision models, confirming its wound healing properties.

formulation/murivenna#204.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/murivenna#204.claimedTitle: Antimicrobial efficacy of Murivenna against common wound pathogens
formulation/murivenna#204.finding: Study from Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham demonstrated broad-spectrum antimicrobial effect against Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli, supporting its use as a wound-protective oil.

formulation/murivenna#205.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/murivenna#205.claimedTitle: Clinical evaluation of Murivenna application on Episiotomy Wound
formulation/murivenna#205.finding: Published in Journal of Ayurveda and Integrated Medical Sciences, Murivenna showed better pain-relieving and tenderness-diminishing properties compared to [Jatyadi Taila](/nighantu/formulation/jatyadi-taila/) in episiotomy wound management in 30 patients.

formulation/mustakarishta#206.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/mustakarishta#207.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/mustakarishta#207.claimedTitle: Comparative account of traditionally fermented biomedicine: Mustakarishta
formulation/mustakarishta#207.finding: Comparative fermentation study confirmed consistent presence of therapeutically active metabolites across traditional and standardized preparation methods.

formulation/mustakarishta#208.claimedTitle: Anti-diarrheal and astringent properties of Cyperus rotundus

formulation/narayana-thailam#209.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/narayana-thailam#209.claimedTitle: Observational study of Narayana Tailam Abhyanga in osteoarthritis
formulation/narayana-thailam#209.finding: Classical sources and modern observational studies note significant reduction in stiffness and swelling in osteoarthritis patients after 21 days of twice-daily Abhyanga with Narayana Tailam.

formulation/narayana-thailam#210.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/narayana-thailam#210.finding: In a pilot trial at Banaras Hindu University, subjects with lower back spasms reported 60% improvement in pain scores after four weeks of nightly oleation and steam fomentation (Swedana) using Narayana Tailam.

formulation/narayana-thailam#211.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/narayana-thailam#211.finding: The [sesame oil](/nighantu/glossary/concepts-m-y/#tila-taila) lipid medium facilitates transdermal delivery of lipophilic phytoconstituents like saponins, lignans, and phenolics, which exert anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/) effects at musculoskeletal target sites.

formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#212.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#212.claimedTitle: Hair growth-promoting activity of Bhringraj and Amla in animal models

formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#213.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#213.claimedTitle: Topical Bhringraj-containing oils and hair density
formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#213.finding: Indian Journal of Dermatology study found that topical use of [Bhringraj](/nighantu/herb/bhringraj/)-containing oils showed significant hair density increase over placebo in 60 subjects over 16 weeks.

formulation/neelibringadi-thailam#214.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/panchagavya-ghrita#215.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/panchagavya-ghrita#215.actualTitle: Panchagavya Ghrita, an Ayurvedic formulation attenuates seizures, cognitive impairment and oxidative stress in pentylenetetrazole induced seizures in rats

formulation/panchagavya-ghrita#217.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/panchagavya-ghrita#217.finding: 25% patients became completely seizure-free; 25% had 50% reduction in seizure frequency; 33.3% had 25% frequency reduction after treatment

formulation/phala-ghrita#230.actualTitle: Clinical trial of phalaghrita on female infertility

formulation/pippali-khanda#235.claimedTitle: Piper longum fruit - comprehensive pharmacological review

formulation/pippali-khanda#236.finding: Classical Vardhamana [Pippali](/nighantu/herb/pippali/) protocol showed improvement in respiratory resilience, digestive strength, and overall vitality in observational clinical setting

formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#256.finding: Published in Journal of Ayurveda & Integrative Medicine, the study showed a 30% reduction in WOMAC pain scores after eight weeks of nightly massage for osteoarthritis patients.

formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#257.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#257.finding: Catechins, tannins, and epicatechol from Sahachara bark were confirmed to deliver astringent and anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis pathways.

formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#258.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#258.claimedTitle: Evaluation of Sahacharadi Thailam in sciatica (Gridhrasi) management
formulation/sahacharadi-thailam#258.finding: Clinical study with 40 patients demonstrated significant reduction in sciatic nerve pain, improvement in straight leg raising test, and reduced disability scores after Kati Basti with [Sahacharadi Thailam](/nighantu/formulation/sahacharadi-thailam/) over 14 sessions.

formulation/sanjivani-vati#259.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sanjivani-vati#259.claimedTitle: Probable Mode of Action of Sanjivani Vati - A Critical Review
formulation/sanjivani-vati#259.finding: Detailed analysis established that drugs in [Sanjivani Vati](/nighantu/formulation/sanjivani-vati/) primarily have Katu and Tikta Rasa with Deepana, Pachana, Anulomana, Jwaraghna, Krimighna, Triptighna, and Vishaghna properties working synergistically for Ama pachana and detoxification.

formulation/sanjivani-vati#260.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sanjivani-vati#260.claimedTitle: Scientific Review on Sanjivani Vati with reference to Pharmacological Actions and Therapeutic Indications
formulation/sanjivani-vati#260.finding: Ingredients demonstrate antimicrobial activities against Salmonella typhi and Helicobacter pylori; formulation works on metabolic processes at cellular level, improving tissue formation and nutrition.

formulation/sanjivani-vati#261.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sanjivani-vati#261.claimedTitle: Sanjivani Vati pharmacological assessment of Amahara and Jwaraghna actions
formulation/sanjivani-vati#261.finding: [Sanjivani Vati](/nighantu/formulation/sanjivani-vati/) shows Amahara action (toxin expulsion) curing diseases from Mandagni (digestive impairment); diaphoretic effect induces perspiration, breaks fever cycle, and averts body temperature rise.

formulation/saraswatarishta#262.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/saraswatarishta#263.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/saraswatarishta#264.finding: Published in Neuroscience Research Notes: identified that phytoconstituents (Withanolide A, 10-[gingerol](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-d-g/#gingerol), Withaferin A) show bioactivity comparable to Bromperidol (dementia/schizophrenia) and Atomoxetine (ADHD).

formulation/sarivadyasava#265.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sarivadyasava#265.claimedTitle: Sarivadyasava as adjuvant in dengue fever management
formulation/sarivadyasava#265.finding: Pilot study in Journal of Ethnopharmacology (n=30): Sarivadyasava plus standard antipyretics vs [antipyretic](/nighantu/reference/antipyretic/) alone - combined therapy group saw faster temperature reduction (average 12 hours earlier).

formulation/sarivadyasava#266.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/sarivadyasava#266.finding: Open-label trial (n=20) in Ayurveda & Health Journal: PASI scores improved by 25% at 4 weeks with reduced itching and scaling.

formulation/sarivadyasava#267.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/shadbindu-taila#268.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/shadbindu-taila#268.actualTitle: Standardization of Shadbindu Taila: An Ayurvedic oil based medicine

formulation/shadbindu-taila#269.finding: In a controlled clinical study, patients receiving [Shadbindu Taila](/nighantu/formulation/shadbindu-taila/) Nasya showed significant improvement in nasal congestion, headache, and facial pain scores, with 70% reporting marked improvement after 30 days of treatment.

formulation/shadbindu-taila#270.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
formulation/shadbindu-taila#270.claimedTitle: Phytochemical profiling and antimicrobial activity of Shadbindu Taila
formulation/shadbindu-taila#270.finding: HPTLC fingerprinting confirmed the presence of kaempferol and other [flavonoids](/nighantu/reference/flavonoids/) with demonstrated antimicrobial activity against common sinus pathogens, supporting its traditional use in sinusitis and ENT disorders.

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#271.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#271.finding: Comprehensive review established that Simhanada [Guggulu](/nighantu/formulation/guggulu/)|Simhanada Guggulu components act as Disease Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs (DMARDs), with Rasa, Guna, Virya, Vipak, and Karma properties working to reduce clinical symptoms of Amavata.

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#272.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#272.finding: Review confirmed antirheumatic, detoxifying, antitoxin, [antimicrobial](/nighantu/reference/antimicrobial/), antipruritic, depurative, laxative, anti-gout, and demulcent qualities with demonstrated ability to reduce inflammation, pain, stiffness, and swelling while improving joint flexibility.

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#273.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/simhanada-guggulu#273.finding: Pharmacognostical characterization and physicochemical standardization provided quality control parameters for commercial preparations.

formulation/sitopaladi-churna#274.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sitopaladi-churna#275.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sitopaladi-churna#277.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sitopaladi-churna#278.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/srikhandasava#279.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/srikhandasava#280.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sudarshan-churna#284.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/sudarshan-churna#284.finding: 25% faster drop in fever among subjects taking 3g twice daily compared to placebo, with additional benefits on appetite and energy restoration.

formulation/sukumara-kashayam#285.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/talisadi-churna#294.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/talisadi-churna#294.finding: Comparative efficacy trial demonstrated comparable cough relief to standard herbal cough syrup but with fewer side effects in the Talisadi group.

formulation/trikatu-churna#297.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/trikatu-churna#297.finding: Piperine from P. nigrum and P. longum enhances bioavailability by up to 2000% for some compounds; [immunomodulatory](/nighantu/reference/immunomodulatory/), antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties additionally confirmed.

formulation/triphala-churna#298.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphala-churna#299.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphala-churna#299.finding: [Triphala](/nighantu/herb/triphala/) promotes growth of beneficial gut bacteria including Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus acidophilus while inhibiting growth of pathogenic bacteria, demonstrating significant prebiotic potential.

formulation/triphala-churna#300.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphala-churna#301.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphala-guggulu#302.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science confirmed anti-obesity potential, though some individual trials showed mixed results on lipid parameters.

formulation/triphala-guggulu#304.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphala-guggulu#305.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

formulation/triphaladi-thailam#306.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kamala#708.claimedTitle: Skin-Whitening Effect of a Callus Extract of Nelumbo nucifera
herb/kamala#708.finding: Clinical trial with 21 volunteers confirmed significant whitening effect of cosmetics containing lotus callus extract, with demonstrated tyrosinase and collagenase inhibition in vitro supporting skin brightening and anti-aging claims.
herb/kamala#708.actualTitle: Skin-Whitening Effect of a Callus Extract of Nelumbo nucifera Isolate Haman

herb/kamala#709.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kampillaka#710.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kampillaka#710.finding: Rottlerin displayed excellent half-life (>2 hours) and oral bioavailability (>35%), superior to other natural phenolics; validated sensitive bioanalytical method (LLOQ: 1.9 ng/mL).

herb/kampillaka#711.claimedTitle: In-vitro Anti-inflammatory Potential of Standardized Rottlerin Enriched Fraction
herb/kampillaka#711.finding: Rottlerin-enriched fraction (70% rottlerin) showed superior COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition compared to reference drugs etoricoxib and ibuprofen.

herb/kampillaka#712.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kampillaka#712.claimedTitle: Cytotoxicity of Rottlerin Against Human Cancer Cell Lines
herb/kampillaka#712.finding: Isolated rottlerin demonstrated significant in vitro cytotoxicity against multiple human cancer cell lines through apoptosis induction.

herb/kamsya-bhasma#713.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kamsya-bhasma#713.claimedTitle: A Brief Review of Kamsya (Bronze) Through Ayurvedic Literature
herb/kamsya-bhasma#713.finding: Comprehensive literature review documented traditional uses, preparation methods, and pharmacological properties. Confirmed that Kamsya formulations are beneficial in Krimi (worm infestations) and Kushta (skin diseases).

herb/kamsya-bhasma#714.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kamsya-bhasma#714.claimedTitle: Therapeutic potentials of metals in ancient India: A review through Charaka Samhita
herb/kamsya-bhasma#714.finding: Historical review confirmed bronze's use since Charaka period for therapeutic instruments and preparations. Cooling properties of Kansa utilized in eye treatments and Pitta-reducing formulations.

herb/kamsya-bhasma#715.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kamsya-bhasma#715.claimedTitle: Exploring the Potential of Ayurvedic Bhasmas as nanomedicine
herb/kamsya-bhasma#715.finding: Bhasma nano-particles (1-2 microns) in [Kamsya Bhasma](/nighantu/herb/kamsya-bhasma/) aid biological systems in assimilation and absorption. The nano-particulate form is considered harmless at therapeutic levels.

herb/kanchanar#716.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kanchanar#716.finding: Registered RCT comparing Kanchanar [Guggulu](/nighantu/formulation/guggulu/) formulation with levothyroxine for hypothyroidism management, with enrollment from June 2024 to December 2025; recognizes growing clinical evidence.
herb/kanchanar#716.actualTitle: Evaluation of Comparative Efficacy of Levothyroxine Versus Kshar Basti and Kanchanar Guggul in the Treatment of Hypothyroidism: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial

herb/kanchanar#717.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kanchanar#717.claimedTitle: Exploring the Therapeutic Potential of Bauhinia variegata: A Review of Botanical, Phytochemical, Pharmacological, and Medicinal Insights
herb/kanchanar#717.finding: Confirmed anti-goitrogenic, hepatoprotective, [immunomodulatory](/nighantu/reference/immunomodulatory/), anti-mutagenic and cytotoxic activities; kaempferol and [quercetin](/nighantu/reference/quercetinquercetin/) identified as key anti-thyroid bioactive constituents.

herb/kanchanar#718.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kanchanar#718.claimedTitle: From LC-MS/MS metabolomics profiling of Kanchanara Guggulu|Kanchanara Guggulu to molecular docking with aldose reductase
herb/kanchanar#718.finding: LC-MS/MS profiling identified [quercetin](/nighantu/reference/quercetinquercetin/) pentaacetate as a potent aldose reductase inhibitor, suggesting additional antidiabetic and anti-cataract potential beyond thyroid applications.
herb/kanchanar#718.actualTitle: From LC-MS/MS metabolomics profiling of Kanchanara Guggulu to molecular docking and dynamics simulation of quercetin pentaacetate with aldose reductase

herb/kankola#719.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kankola#719.finding: Comprehensive review documenting lignans as the main active constituents with cubebin as the most abundant; validated antioxidant, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and [anticancer](/nighantu/reference/anticancer/) effects.

herb/kankola#720.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kankola#720.claimedTitle: Cubeb (Piper cubeba L.): nutritional value, phytochemical profiling and dermacosmeceutical properties
herb/kankola#720.finding: Identified novel dermacosmeceutical applications of cubeb extracts with documented antioxidant, anti-aging, and skin-protective properties alongside nutritional value.
herb/kankola#720.actualTitle: Cubeb (Piper cubeba L.): nutritional value, phytochemical profiling and dermacosmeceutical properties

herb/kankola#721.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kankola#721.claimedTitle: Extraction and Phytochemical Screening of Kankola (Piper cubeba) for in-vitro Antidiabetic Potential
herb/kankola#721.finding: Demonstrated significant in vitro antidiabetic potential through alpha-amylase and alpha-glucosidase inhibition assays.

herb/kankshi#722.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kankshi#722.claimedTitle: The traditional uses, phytochemistry and pharmacology of Abrus precatorius L.: A comprehensive review
herb/kankshi#722.finding: Identified over 166 chemical compounds covering flavonoids, phenolics, [terpenoids](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-t-z/#terpenoids), [alkaloids](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids), and [proteins](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-o-q/#proteins); documented wide range of pharmacological functions including antitumor, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory activities.
herb/kankshi#722.actualTitle: The traditional uses, phytochemistry and pharmacology of Abrus precatorius L.: A comprehensive review

herb/kankshi#723.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kankshi#723.claimedTitle: Abrus precatorius: A deep insight into ethnobotanical, phytochemistry and pharmacology
herb/kankshi#723.finding: Comprehensive review documenting antimicrobial, [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/), and [hepatoprotective](/nighantu/reference/hepatoprotective/) activities of various plant parts, with emphasis on the differential toxicity between seed coat and kernel.

herb/kankshi#724.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kankshi#724.claimedTitle: Abrus precatorius: comprehensive insight into phytochemical, therapeutic activities and safety
herb/kankshi#724.finding: Established that the hard seed coat significantly reduces toxicity of intact seeds; ingestion of whole uncrushed seeds typically results in only mild symptoms and complete recovery.

herb/kanmad-bhasma#725.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kanmad-bhasma#725.claimedTitle: Structural investigation of Ayurveda Lauha (Iron) Bhasma - magnetic property studies
herb/kanmad-bhasma#725.finding: Lauha Bhasma from magnetite has great potential for noninvasive localized target killing of cancer cells via necrosis by application of alternating external magnetic field or photoelectron generation through X-rays.

herb/kanmad-bhasma#725.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

herb/kanmad-bhasma#726.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kanmad-bhasma#726.claimedTitle: Crystal Structure and Magnetic Property Studies on Nanocrystalline Lauh (Iron) Bhasma
herb/kanmad-bhasma#726.finding: Confirmed nanocrystalline form with both magnetic and luminescence properties. Can be employed as magnetic material for various technological applications beyond traditional medicine.

herb/kanmad-bhasma#727.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kanmad-bhasma#727.claimedTitle: A Review on Kanta Loha (Magnetite) - Comprehensive literature analysis
herb/kanmad-bhasma#727.finding: Kanta Loha is the best variety of iron per Rasa Shastra texts. Must contain at least 60% iron and not exceed specified heavy metal limits. Effective against anemia, diabetes, and chronic fevers.

herb/kantakari#728.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kantakari#728.claimedTitle: A Systematic Review on Solanum xanthocarpum L. (Solanaceae) Plant and Its Potential Pharmacological Activities
herb/kantakari#728.finding: Systematic evaluation confirmed larvicidal, antibacterial, antihyperglycemic, [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/), and hepatoprotective activities with significant [bronchodilator](/nighantu/reference/bronchodilator/) potential.

herb/kantakari#729.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kantakari#729.claimedTitle: Phytochemical and Pharmacological Activities of Solanum surattense
herb/kantakari#729.finding: Extract showed significant bronchodilator activity on histamine-induced airway constriction and reversed allergen-induced bronchospasm comparable to standard aminophylline.

herb/kantakari#730.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kantakari#730.claimedTitle: Morphology and Phytochemistry of Solanum xanthocarpum
herb/kantakari#730.finding: Detailed phytochemical mapping identified solanocarpine, solanocarpidine, and diosgenin as primary steroidal constituents with anti-inflammatory and [immunomodulatory](/nighantu/reference/immunomodulatory/) activity.

herb/kapittha#731.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/kapittha#731.finding: Comprehensive review documented [anticancer](/nighantu/reference/anticancer/), antidiabetic, anti-diarrheal, antimicrobial, antiulcer, wound healing, antioxidant, hepatoprotective, [neuroprotective](/nighantu/reference/neuroprotective/), antispermatogenic, [diuretic](/nighantu/reference/diuretic/), and adsorbent activities.

herb/kapittha#732.finding: Rich chemical composition including quinones, [lignans](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-g-l/#lignans), [flavonoids](/nighantu/reference/flavonoids/), [sterols](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sterols), coumarins, [alkaloids](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids), [triterpenoids](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-t-z/#triterpenoids), phenolic acids and volatile oils were characterized across all plant parts.

herb/kapittha#733.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/kapittha#733.claimedTitle: Bioactive Compounds of Wood Apple (Limonia acidissima L.)
herb/kapittha#733.finding: Fruit shell coumarins (osthenol, psoralen, xanthotoxin) demonstrated potent antifungal activity against common dermatophytes, validating traditional use for skin infections.

herb/karanja#734.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/karanja#734.claimedTitle: Karanja (Milletia pinnata (L.) Panigrahi): a tropical tree with varied applications
herb/karanja#734.finding: Comprehensive review documented [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/), antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, cytotoxicity and [immunomodulatory](/nighantu/reference/immunomodulatory/) activities; identified karanjin and pongamol as compounds with most promising biological activities.

herb/karanja#735.finding: Validated multiple traditional uses including anti-dermatosis, wound healing and anti-hemorrhoidal applications; seed oil demonstrated significant antibacterial activity against skin pathogens.

herb/kasis-bhasma#754.finding: [Kasis Bhasma](/nighantu/herb/kasis-bhasma/) improved hemoglobin levels and ferritin without the gastrointestinal side effects commonly seen with conventional ferrous sulfate supplementation.

herb/kasturi#755.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/naga-bhasma#889.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?

herb/rakta-chandana#987.claimedTitle: Wound Healing Potential of Pterocarpus santalinus Linn: A Pharmacological Evaluation
herb/rakta-chandana#987.finding: Red sandalwood ointment significantly accelerated wound healing in punch and burn wound models, with enhanced collagenesis and supporting biochemical data in both normal and diabetic rats.
herb/rakta-chandana#987.actualTitle: Wound healing potential of Pterocarpus santalinus linn: a pharmacological evaluation
herb/rakta-chandana#987.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds

herb/rakta-chandana#988.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rakta-chandana#988.claimedTitle: Pterocarpus santalinus Selectively Inhibits Pro-Inflammatory Genes in IL-1 Stimulated Endothelial Cells
herb/rakta-chandana#988.finding: Red sandalwood extract selectively inhibited a subset of pro-inflammatory gene expression in IL-1 stimulated endothelial cells, demonstrating targeted anti-inflammatory activity relevant to inflammatory skin conditions.
herb/rakta-chandana#988.actualTitle: Pterocarpus santalinus Selectively Inhibits a Subset of Pro-Inflammatory Genes in Interleukin-1 Stimulated Endothelial Cells

herb/rasamanikya#989.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasamanikya#989.claimedTitle: Acute and chronic toxicity of Rasamanikya - an Ayurvedic arsenical formulation in rats
herb/rasamanikya#989.finding: Haratal Bhasma and Raw Haratal exhibited nearly non-toxicological profile when administered in specific doses, attributed to arsenic being in a compound sulfide form that is insoluble in the human body. However, systematic toxicity studies are limited.

herb/rasamanikya#990.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasamanikya#990.finding: Established standardized manufacturing procedures. Shodhana significantly reduced arsenic content compared to raw orpiment. ICP-AES confirmed arsenic and sulfur as major constituents. Different preparation methods yielded products with varying arsenic concentrations.

herb/rasamanikya#991.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasamanikya#991.claimedTitle: Rasamanikya clinical safety pilot study in healthy volunteers
herb/rasamanikya#991.finding: Ten healthy volunteers administered Rasamanikya for 15 consecutive days showed significantly increased arsenic levels in blood without any signs of clinical toxicity, suggesting that the processed sulfide form has different pharmacokinetics than inorganic arsenicals.

herb/rasna#992.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasna#992.claimedTitle: Pluchea lanceolata (Rasana): Chemical and Biological Potential of Rasayana Herb Used in Traditional System of Medicine
herb/rasna#992.finding: Documented triterpenoids, [sterols](/nighantu/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sterols), flavonoids and lactones as prominent constituents; validated anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and immunomodulatory activities.
herb/rasna#992.actualTitle: Pluchea lanceolata (Rasana): Chemical and biological potential of Rasayana herb used in traditional system of medicine

herb/rasna#993.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasna#993.claimedTitle: Comparative Pharmacognostic and Phytochemical Analysis of Three Market Samples of Rasna
herb/rasna#993.finding: Comparative study of Pluchea lanceolata, Alpinia officinarum, and Alpinia calcarata established distinctive phytochemical markers for quality control and authentication.

herb/rasna#994.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasna#994.claimedTitle: Current Pharmacological and Phytochemical Studies of Alpinia galanga
herb/rasna#994.finding: Alpinia galanga rhizome extracts demonstrated anti-cancer, [antioxidant](/nighantu/reference/antioxidant/), antibacterial, antiviral, cardiovascular protective, and digestive system protective effects.
herb/rasna#994.actualTitle: Current pharmacological and phytochemical studies of the plant Alpinia galanga
herb/rasna#994.journal: Zhong xi yi jie he xue bao = Journal of Chinese integrative medicine

herb/rasona-garlic#995.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasona-garlic#995.claimedTitle: Garlic bioactive substances and their therapeutic applications for improving human health: a comprehensive review
herb/rasona-garlic#995.finding: Comprehensive review documenting allicin's role in cardiovascular protection, antioxidant effects through NADPH oxidase inhibition, and direct ROS scavenging within cells.
herb/rasona-garlic#995.actualTitle: Garlic bioactive substances and their therapeutic applications for improving human health: a comprehensive review

herb/rasona-garlic#996.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasona-garlic#996.claimedTitle: Traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology and toxicology of garlic (Allium sativum): A review of research from the last decade
herb/rasona-garlic#996.finding: Decade-long research review establishing antioxidant, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, antihyperlipidemic, [anticancer](/nighantu/reference/anticancer/), antimicrobial, [hepatoprotective](/nighantu/reference/hepatoprotective/), and immunostimulant activities.
herb/rasona-garlic#996.actualTitle: Traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology and toxicology of garlic (Allium sativum), a storehouse of diverse phytochemicals: A review of research from the last decade focusing on health and nutritional implications

herb/rasona-garlic#997.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasona-garlic#997.claimedTitle: Valorization of garlic (Allium sativum L.) byproducts: Bioactive compounds, biological properties, and applications
herb/rasona-garlic#997.finding: Garlic byproducts (leaves, stems, outer skin) contain significant bioactive compounds with antioxidant and antimicrobial properties, supporting waste-to-value applications.
herb/rasona-garlic#997.actualTitle: Valorization of garlic (Allium sativum L.) byproducts: Bioactive compounds, biological properties, and applications

herb/rasona-patra#998.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasona-patra#998.claimedTitle: Valorization of garlic (Allium sativum L.) byproducts: Bioactive compounds, biological properties, and applications
herb/rasona-patra#998.finding: Garlic leaves and stems contain significant bioactive sulfur compounds, flavonoids, and phenolic acids with demonstrated antioxidant and antimicrobial properties, establishing their value as functional food ingredients.
herb/rasona-patra#998.actualTitle: Valorization of garlic (Allium sativum L.) byproducts: Bioactive compounds, biological properties, and applications

herb/rasona-patra#999.heading: What do recent clinical trials show?
herb/rasona-patra#999.claimedTitle: Chemical Constituents and Pharmacological Activities of Garlic (Allium sativum L.): A Review
herb/rasona-patra#999.finding: All parts of garlic including leaves contain organosulfur compounds with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities, though bulb preparations have been more extensively studied.
